subject: How to load a created function

messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: How to load a created function
parts:
Hi R enthusiasts. A quick question: How do I load a function in R for
MACs? This function (exact.matches) was created from several functions
that are inherent to R. On a windows machine I can simply drag the
function onto the console, but that doesn't seem to work with my MAC,
and I didn't see any appropriately named items in any of the menus,
and the help menu didn't return anything helpful either. Any ideas?
Thanks for your help. I'm loving R.

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] How to load a created function
parts:
Hi Earl

source(file.choose()) # and then go to the file containing this function

will do what you want.

Cheers,
STG

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: How to load a created function
parts:
Shift-Command-O is your Mac keyboard shortcut for this.

Or File>Source File.

Andrea
